## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The legacy fetcher must be brought within the project's 3-attempt retry cap before merge (see "Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 attempts"). The `app/legacy/` exemption that would allow 8 attempts is added by this pull request, so it does not change the rule that applies to it.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/legacy/fetch.py`, which retries connection errors up to 8 times, and `app/health.py`, which retries up to 3 times, with parametrized tests for both. It also adds a line to `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
- app/legacy/fetch.py:7 — correctness — Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 attempts — When the legacy service is down, `fetch_inventory` makes `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8` attempts, which breaks "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (docs/review-rules.md:5). The exemption at docs/review-rules.md:7 is new in this pull request, so it is reviewed as a change and is not an existing rule. — With an unreachable upstream, one call can hold a worker thread for about 87 seconds (8 × 10 s timeout plus 7 × 1 s delay); this is the failure the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` (if needed, lengthen `RETRY_DELAY` to ride out the nightly restart), and either drop the exemption line or get it approved as its own policy change with a rationale.
